cards.explanation: The answer is False. Nahum says it plainly: “The LORD is slow to anger and great in power…” That sits in the same breath as the avenging and the wrath. Slow to anger is a very different thing from quick to anger. A quick-tempered person has hair-trigger anger, and that isn't the picture Nahum paints.

The answer is that He will surely punish them. Right after calling Him slow to anger, Nahum says, “the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished.” Slow to anger doesn't mean the guilty get a pass. Both things are true of Him at the same time, friends.

The answer is that it wilts. Verse 4 says, “Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.” Bashan and Carmel are places, and they wither in the same verse. Just before that, “He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry.”

The answer is that they quake before Him. Nahum says, “The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away…” Mountains are the biggest, steadiest things around, and they shake when the LORD is there. If they quake, I'd be shaking in my apron, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 6 says, “His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.” Rocks are about the toughest thing you can name. When even they shatter, that tells you how great His power is, friends.

The answer is those who trust in Him. Verse 7 says, “The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him.” Right after the storm and fire, Nahum puts the focus on trust. That's a lot of comfort packed into one line, friends.
The answer is False. Nahum says He will “…pursue His enemies into darkness.” Pursuing is the opposite of letting someone escape. It's a serious line, and Nahum doesn't soften it.

The answer is that affliction will not rise up a second time. Verse 9 says, “Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end.” Then it adds, “Affliction will not rise up a second time.” That's the promise: no second round of affliction.

The answer is dry. Nahum says they'll be consumed “…like stubble that is fully dry.” The word is fully dry, not just a little dry. Think of a crumb that's been sitting out so long it crunches when you look at it, friends.

The answer is that they will be cut down and gone. The LORD says, “Though they are allied and numerous, yet they will be cut down and pass away.” Allied and numerous sounds like a big crowd with backup. The LORD says it still won't matter, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Though I have afflicted you, O Judah, I will afflict you no longer.” Judah is the kingdom that stayed with David's family (1 Kings 12:20). After Nineveh's bad news, this is a gentle turn for Judah, friends.

The answer is tear away. The LORD says, “For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.” Break the yoke and tear away the shackles. Those are both things coming off Judah, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD's command says, “There will be no descendants to carry on your name.” That's what He says about Nineveh. It's a heavy word, and Nahum doesn't soften it.

The answer is its grave. In verse 14 the LORD says, “I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.” The LORD gives the reason right in the verse. It's a heavy line, and Nahum just states it plainly.

The answer is to celebrate your feasts. Nahum says, “Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows.” With good news on the way, Judah is told to celebrate. That's one of my favorite lines in the whole chapter, friends.

The answer is True. Nahum says, “For the wicked will never again march through you; they will be utterly cut off.” Never again is a big promise. That's good news for Judah, and it's the kind of line you'd tell a friend.
